name.description: Return states with this exact name, compared case-insensitively. In an ungoverned workspace, several projects can each have a state with the same name.

group.description: Return only states in this workflow group. One of `backlog`, `unstarted`, `started`, `completed`, `cancelled`, or `triage`. Use `group__in` to match several groups at once, comma-separated: `?group__in=started,completed`. `triage` is accepted but never matches, because this route leaves out every state in the `triage` group.

is-default.description: Return only the project's default state (`true`) or only the non-default states (`false`). Pairing `?is_default=true` with `?per_page=1` is the cheapest way to find where new work items will land.

external-source.description: Return states that came from a particular system, for example `jira`. Combine it with `external_id`, because an `external_id` is unique only within its source.

search.description: A search term matched against the state name.

order-by.description: Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `sequence` , `-sequence`: the project's own workflow order - `created_at` , `-created_at`: when each state was added - `id` , `-id` Order by `sequence` when you are rendering the workflow to a user; it is the order the project itself uses.

per-page.description: Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. Most projects have fewer than 20 states, so one page is usually the whole workflow.

offset.description: Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Use the `next` value from the response instead of computing offsets yourself.

paginate.description: Set to `cursor` to switch to the keyset envelope, which skips the `COUNT` query and returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Leave it out to get the default offset envelope.

count.description: Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT(*)` behind `total_count`; the field is then omitted from the response.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Fields you don't request are left out of the response instead of coming back as `null`, so a missing key means you didn't ask for it and `null` means the value is null. `id` is always included, whether or not you name it. Pass `all` to get every requestable field. An unknown field name returns `400` with the list of valid names and the closest match, so a typo is caught instead of being silently ignored. Requestable here: `color`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `group`, `id`, `is_default`, `is_triage`, `name`, `sequence`, `updated_at`, `updated_by_id`. See [Sparse fields](/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields).

filter-project.description: Return only the states of this project. It matches rows only in an ungoverned workspace, because catalog states have no project.

name.description: New display name, unique within the project. Maximum 255 characters. Renaming is safe for reporting, because boards and charts use `group`, not `name`.

group.description: Move the state to a different workflow group. This changes how every work item in the state is counted by boards, charts, and cycle progress, so switching a state from `started` to `completed` retroactively changes how those work items are reported. - `backlog`: not yet scheduled - `unstarted`: scheduled but not begun - `started`: actively in progress - `completed`: finished successfully - `cancelled`: closed without completion - `triage`: awaiting intake review

sequence.description: Ordering weight within the project. Lower values sort first. Set it to reposition the state in the workflow.

is_default.description: Make this the project's default state, the one work items land in when no `state_id` is supplied. A project has exactly one default, so setting this to `true` clears the flag on the state that held it.

external_id.description: Your system's identifier for this state, for sync and import correlation. Maximum 255 characters.

external_source.description: The system `external_id` came from, for example `github` or `jira`. Maximum 255 characters.
